newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tajikistan PM says IMF economic targets achieved.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan PM says IMF economic targets achieved.

text.p: The Republic of Tajikistan is meeting economic targets set in a credit agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) earlier this year, Prime Minister Yakhyo Azimov said on Wednesday.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Azimov said inflation had fallen below a four percent target by the end of September. He also noted that a fiscal imbalance had been reduced.
The IMF approved a first credit tranche totalling US$22 million to Tajikistan in May.

The agreement was designed to help support Tajikistan's economic reform programme, which includes reducing inflation to about four percent, building foreign reserves, and slowing down a decline in output and real income.
"At the present moment, all the requirements for foreign reserves have been met by us," Asimov said.
"One of the first activities of the government is the acceleration of the transition to a market economy," Azimov said, noting that Tajikistan had already developed a stock exchange.

"A priority is to establish a legal basis in order to provide investors with specific privileges in order to secure their investment," he said, noting that the government would work to privatise its agricultural industry.
Azimov and the prime ministers of Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan are in Tokyo to attend a World Bank conference on investment in central Asia this week.
